title: The coherent nerve of a locally Kan simplicial category is a quasicategory
statement: Use simplicial sets from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], horns, quasicategories and Kan complexes from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and simplicial categories, the subset-poset simplicial categories $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, the coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ and the simplicial categories $\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $A$ be a simplicial category, in a universe containing its objects and mapping simplicial sets, such that every morphism simplicial set $A(x,y)$ is a Kan complex. Then its coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$, whose $n$-simplices are the simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to A$ with simplicial operators given by restriction, is a quasicategory: every map $\Lambda_i^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(A)$ with $0<i<n$ extends to $\Delta^n$. In particular, for every universe $\mathcal W$, the infinity category of spaces $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W})$, whose morphism simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(S,T)$ are Kan complexes, is a quasicategory.
